data.content_ref: inline:The claim asserts a necessity: the preference is defensible 'only if' rationality is redefined as fidelity to the critical method. But the artifact's own second countercondition describes a scenario in which rule-following inherently implies belief in the utility of the rules, thereby reintroducing induction. If induction is reintroduced, the preference connects to truth-optimization through standard rationality — no redefinition required. This directly falsifies the 'only if': there exists a path (countercondition 2) under which the preference is defensible without redefining rationality at all. The claim's modal strength is inconsistent with its own enumerated escape routes.
